frames.t: 私 ___ {role} です

w.が: が would stress “me, not someone else”. Saying who you are uses は.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on, and です isn't that kind of verb.
w.で: で marks where or how an action happens. Nothing is happening here.

frames.use: は · asking about a known thing
frames.t: {pl} ___ どこ です か
frames.n: You're asking about something already known, so it's the topic.

w.が: Before どこ, the thing you're asking about is already known, so it takes は.
w.を: を needs an action verb.
w.に: に would go on the place in the answer, not on the thing you're asking about.

frames.t: 今日 ___ 雨 です

w.が: 今日が would single today out from other days. As the topic of the sentence, use は.
w.を: を needs an action verb, and です isn't one.
w.で: で marks the place or means of an action.

frames.t: 肉 は 食べます が 、 魚 ___ 食べません
frames.en: I eat meat, but fish I don't eat.
frames.n: は sets fish against meat.

w.が: The sentence sets fish against meat. Contrast is は's job.
w.で: で would mean you eat by means of fish.
w.に: に marks a destination or a time, and fish is neither.

frames.t: {who} ___ 来ました

w.は: は would treat the person as a known topic. Reporting who came, as news, uses が.
w.を: を marks what's acted on, but this person does the coming.
w.で: で marks a place or means, not who acts.

frames.t: 机 の 上 に {item} ___ あります
frames.n: New information about what exists takes が.

w.は: は would treat it as already known. Here you're introducing it as new.
w.を: あります doesn't act on anything, so it takes no を.
w.で: With あります, the place takes に and the thing takes が.

frames.t: 公園 に {animal} ___ います

w.は: は would treat it as already known. Here you're introducing it as new.
w.を: います doesn't act on anything, so it takes no を.

frames.t: 私 は {like} ___ 好き です
frames.n: 好き is an adjective in Japanese, so what you like takes が.

w.は: With 好き, the thing you like takes が. The person already has は.
w.を: 好き is an adjective, not a verb, so it doesn't take を.
w.で: で marks a place or means of an action.

frames.t: だれ ___ 来ました か
frames.n: Question words like だれ always take が, never は.

w.は: Question words can't be the topic, so だれ can't take は.
w.を: を would mean someone came and was acted on. だれ does the coming.

frames.t: 友達 は {lang} ___ 上手 です

w.は: With 上手, the skill takes が. The person already has は.
w.を: 上手 is an adjective, so it doesn't take を.
w.で: で would mean “by means of”.

frames.t: {lang} ___ 分かります
frames.n: 分かります takes が, even though English makes it an object.

w.は: With 分かります, what you understand takes が.
w.を: This is a common mistake. 分かります takes が, not を.
w.で: で would mean “by means of” the language.

frames.t: {food} ___ 食べます

w.が: が would make the food the one doing the eating.

frames.t: {drink} ___ 飲みます

w.に: に marks a destination or a time. Drinks are what the verb acts on.
w.で: で marks a place or means, not what's drunk.

frames.t: {read} ___ 読みます

w.が: が would make it the one doing the reading.

frames.t: 音楽 ___ 聞きます

w.が: が would make the music the listener.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: テレビ ___ 見ます

w.に: に marks a destination or a time.
w.が: が would make the TV the one watching.

frames.t: {lang} ___ 勉強します

w.に: に marks a destination or a time.

frames.t: 道 ___ 歩きます
frames.n: With movement verbs, を marks the route.

w.へ: へ would mean walking toward the road, not along it.
w.が: が would make the road the one walking.

frames.t: バス ___ 降ります
frames.n: You leave the bus, so it takes を. Getting on takes に.

w.に: に is for getting on, as in バスに乗ります.
w.が: が would make the bus the one getting off.

frames.t: {pl} ___ 行きます
frames.n: へ also works here.

w.を: Going doesn't act on the place. Use に for where you're heading.
w.で: で marks where an action happens, not where you're going.

frames.t: {clock} ___ 起きます

w.で: で marks a place or means, not a time.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: {day} ___ 休みます

w.で: で marks a place or means, not a day.
w.を: を would treat the day as what you rest from, which needs a different sentence.

frames.t: 部屋 ___ {animal} が います
frames.n: います and あります take に for the place.

w.で: で is for where an action happens. Existing takes に.
w.を: を needs a verb that acts on something.

frames.t: {to} ___ 手紙 を 書きます

w.で: で marks a place or means, not who receives it.
w.が: が would make this person the writer.

frames.t: {ride} ___ 乗ります

w.を: 乗ります takes に. を is for getting off, with 降ります.
w.で: で would mean riding somewhere by this vehicle, which needs a different verb phrase.

frames.t: {to} ___ 会います
frames.n: This is a common mistake for English speakers, since “meet” looks like it needs を. と also works.

w.を: 会います doesn't take を. Use に for the person.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: {study} ___ 勉強します

w.に: に marks a destination or where something exists. For an action, use で.
w.を: を would make the place the subject you study.

frames.t: {eat} ___ 昼ご飯 を 食べます

w.に: に marks a destination or where something exists. For an action, use で.

frames.t: {by} ___ 行きます

w.を: を would mean going along it as a route, not using it.
w.が: が would make the vehicle the one going.

frames.t: はし ___ 食べます

w.を: を would mean you're eating the chopsticks.
w.に: に marks a destination or a time.

frames.t: 日本語 ___ 話します

w.に: に marks a destination or a time.

frames.t: ペン ___ 書きます

w.を: を would mean the pen is what you're writing.

frames.t: {country} ___ 行きます
frames.n: に also works here.

w.を: Going doesn't act on the place.
w.で: で marks where an action happens, not where you're heading.

frames.t: どこ ___ 行きます か
frames.n: に also works here.

w.を: Going doesn't act on the place.
w.が: が would mean “which place is going?”

frames.t: 来年 {country} ___ 帰ります
frames.en: I'm going back to {country} next year.
frames.n: に also works here.

w.を: Returning doesn't act on the place.
w.で: で marks where an action happens.

frames.t: 私 ___ {own} です

w.を: を needs a verb to act on it. These are two nouns to link.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: {lang} ___ 先生 です

w.を: を needs a verb to act on it. These are two nouns to link.
w.に: に marks a destination or a time.

frames.t: 友達 ___ 名前 は 何 です か

w.を: を needs a verb to act on it. These are two nouns to link.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: 机 ___ 上 に {item} が あります
frames.n: 机の上 is “the top of the desk”.

w.を: を needs a verb to act on it.
w.で: で marks where an action happens.

frames.t: 私 ___ {role} です

w.と: と means “with” or “and”, and there's nothing to join it to here. “Too” is も.
w.は: は is grammatical, but it loses the “too”.
w.を: を needs an action verb.

frames.t: {food} ___ 食べます
frames.n: も replaces を here.

w.と: と would need a second food after it. “Too” is も.
w.を: を is grammatical, but it loses the “too”.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: 友達 ___ 来ました

w.と: 友達 と 来ました means you came with a friend. The English says the friend came too: も.
w.が: が is grammatical, but it loses the “too”.
w.を: を marks what's acted on, but the friend does the coming.

frames.t: 何 ___ 食べませんでした
frames.n: A question word plus も with a negative verb means “not any”.

w.と: 何 と doesn't work here. A question word plus も with a negative means “nothing”.
w.を: 何を would ask “what”, and this isn't a question.
w.が: 何が would ask “what” as the subject.

frames.t: {to} ___ 話します

w.も: も would mean you talk to them as well as others. “With” is と.
w.を: を would make the person what you're saying.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: パン ___ 卵 を 食べます
frames.n: と lists everything. や means “among other things”.

w.も: も doesn't join two nouns. “Bread and eggs” is パン と 卵.
w.で: で would mean eating eggs by means of bread.
w.を: を can't link two nouns.

frames.t: {to} ___ {country} へ 行きます

w.も: も would mean they are going too. The English says you go with them, which is と.
w.を: Going doesn't act on a person.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: 父 ___ 母 は 家 に います
frames.en: My father and mother are at home.

w.も: も doesn't join two nouns. “Father and mother” is 父 と 母.
w.を: を can't link two nouns.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: これ は 本 です ___

w.ね: ね would assume it's a book and ask you to agree. To really ask, use か.
w.を: を can't end a sentence here.
w.の: の links two nouns. To ask a polite question, use か.

frames.t: 今 何時 です ___

w.ね: ね looks for agreement. This is a real question.
w.を: を can't end a sentence here.

frames.t: コーヒー ___ お茶 を 飲みます

w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: いい 天気 です ___
frames.n: ね invites the other person to agree.

w.か: か would ask whether the weather is nice. Here you're inviting agreement.
w.を: を can't end a sentence here.

frames.t: 九時 ___ 五時 まで 働きます

w.まで: まで marks the end point. The start takes から.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: 駅 ___ 学校 まで 歩きます
frames.en: I walk from the station to school.

w.まで: まで marks the end point. The start takes から.
w.に: に marks a destination, but this is where you start.

frames.use: から · where you come from
frames.t: {country} ___ 来ました

w.で: で marks where an action happens, not where you came from.
w.を: を isn't used for where someone comes from with 来ました.

frames.t: 九時 から 五時 ___ 働きます

w.から: から marks the start. The end takes まで.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: 駅 ___ 歩きます
frames.en: I walk as far as the station.

w.から: から would mean walking from the station.
w.で: で would mean walking around at the station.

frames.t: 何時 ___ 働きます か
frames.en: Until what time do you work?

w.から: から would ask when you start.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: パン ___ 卵 など を 買います
frames.en: I buy things like bread and eggs.
frames.n: や gives examples from a longer list.

w.で: で would mean buying by means of bread.
w.を: を can't link two nouns.

frames.t: 机 の 上 に 本 ___ ノート が あります
frames.en: On the desk are books, notebooks and so on.

w.を: を can't link two nouns.
w.で: で marks a place or means.

frames.t: これ ___ 何 です か

w.が: これが would ask which one is the what. You're asking about the thing in front of you, so it's the topic.
w.を: を needs an action verb.

frames.t: {lang} ___ 難しい です

w.が: が would single it out from other languages. A general statement about it uses は.
w.を: 難しい is an adjective, so no を.

frames.t: 私 ___ 毎朝 コーヒー を 飲みます

w.が: が would stress “me, not someone else”. Talking about your habits uses は.
w.を: を already marks the coffee.

frames.t: 日曜日 ___ 休み です

w.が: が would answer “which day is your day off?”. Here Sunday is the topic.
w.に: に marks the time of an action, and です isn't an action.

frames.t: 肉 は 好き です が 、 魚 ___ 好き じゃ ありません
frames.en: I like meat, but I don't like fish.
frames.n: は sets fish against meat.

w.が: The sentence sets fish against meat. Contrast is は's job.
w.を: 好き is an adjective, so it doesn't take を.

frames.t: どれ ___ あなた の 傘 です か
frames.n: Question words take が, never は.

w.は: Question words like どれ can't be the topic, so they take が.
w.を: を needs an action verb.

frames.t: 何 ___ 好き です か

w.は: Question words can't be the topic, so 何 takes が.
w.を: 好き is an adjective, so it doesn't take を.

frames.t: 近く に 駅 ___ あります か

w.は: は would treat the station as already known. You're asking whether one exists, so use が.
w.で: With あります, the place takes に and the thing takes が.

frames.t: {country} ___ 住んで います
frames.n: 住む takes に for where you live.

w.で: で marks where an action happens. Living somewhere takes に.
w.を: を needs a verb that acts on something.

frames.t: かばん ___ 本 を 入れます
frames.en: I put a book in my bag.

w.で: で would mean the bag is where you do the putting. Where the book ends up takes に.
w.が: が would make the bag the one doing it.

frames.t: 駅 ___ 友達 を 待ちます
frames.en: I wait for my friend at the station.

w.に: Waiting is an action, so its place takes で, not に.
w.を: を already marks your friend.

frames.t: {pl} ___ 働きます

w.に: Working is an action, so its place takes で.
w.を: を would make the place what you work on.

frames.t: 友達 ___ 映画 を 見ました
frames.en: I watched a movie with a friend.

w.も: 友達 も would mean your friend watched it too. “With” is と.
w.を: を already marks the movie.

frames.t: 母 ___ 電話 で 話しました
frames.en: I talked with my mother on the phone.

w.も: 母 も would mean your mother talked too. “With” is と.
w.を: を would make your mother what you said.

frames.t: 明日 ___ 雨 です

w.と: と can't join 明日 to the rest. “Too” is も.
w.を: を needs an action verb.

frames.t: だれ ___ いません
frames.n: A question word plus も with a negative verb means “no one”.

w.と: だれ と means “with whom”, and this isn't a question.
w.が: だれ が would ask “who?”

frames.t: 授業 は 何時 ___ です か

w.まで: まで would ask when it ends.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: 家 ___ 駅 まで 歩きます
frames.en: I walk from home to the station.

w.まで: まで marks the end point. The start takes から.
w.を: を with a walking verb marks the route, not the start.

frames.t: 月曜日 ___ 金曜日 まで 働きます

w.まで: まで marks the end. The first day takes から.
w.に: に marks a single day, not a starting point.

frames.use: から · where it comes from
frames.t: {country} ___ 手紙 が 来ました

w.まで: まで would mean “as far as”.
w.で: で marks where an action happens.

frames.t: 家 から 学校 ___ バス で 行きます
frames.en: I go from home to school by bus.

w.から: から marks the start. After it, the end takes まで.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: 五時 ___ 待ちます

w.から: から would mean waiting from 5:00 on.
w.に: に would mean at 5:00 exactly, not until.

frames.t: 金曜日 ___ 休み です

w.から: から would mean off starting Friday.
w.を: を marks what a verb acts on.

frames.t: あなた は 学生 です ___

w.ね: ね assumes the answer and asks you to agree. To really ask, use か.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: トイレ は どこ です ___

w.ね: A question word like どこ needs か to make a question.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: いっしょ に 行きません ___
frames.n: 〜ませんか is a polite invitation.

w.ね: 行きませんね would mean “you're not going, are you?”
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: これ は いくら です ___

w.ね: A question word like いくら needs か to make a question.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: 今日 は 暑い です ___

w.か: か would really ask whether it's hot, though you can both feel it.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: この すし は おいしい です ___
frames.en: This sushi is delicious, isn't it?

w.か: か would ask whether it's delicious. Here you're sharing what you both taste.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: 日本語 が 上手 です ___

w.か: か would ask whether their Japanese is good, which sounds doubtful.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: 寒い です ___

w.か: か would ask whether it's cold. ね shares the feeling.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.

frames.t: 明日 は 休み です ___
frames.n: ね checks something you think is true.

w.か: か asks without assuming. ね checks what you think you know.
w.を: を can't end a sentence.
